items.title: Slide Hampton interviewed by Monk Rowe, West Orange, New Jersey, July 30, 2003
items.q: So there were several guys that were writing a lot. Willie Maiden and Don Sebesky and a couple of other guys that were in the band.

ctx.x: “Mark of Jazz.” Yeah. You were writing hot licks way back then too.

Yeah. Maynard gave us a lot of opportunity to arrange and to learn about arranging. So we were inspired writing there in that band. So there were several guys that were writing a lot. Willie Maiden and Don Sebesky and a couple of other guys that were in the band. Then we were playing arrangements by great arrangers from other bands too.

items.title: Slide Hampton — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Don was a smart enough man to know that the best thing for us to do in there was try to make our styles match.

ctx.x: I probably was. It was the first arrangement that I wrote for Maynard. I guess we didn’t have any blues in the band at that time. So I was going to write a blues. But it didn’t have a lot of a blues flavor in it. But I wrote it in one night, and they liked it. So we played it.
Let’s go back to – you were next to Don Sebesky in that band.
